headline: Metro services suspended for 26 mins after cabin door opens mid-journey
summary: A Motijheel-bound train's operator cabin door opened due to heavy passenger pressure in the women's coach, causing a brief service disruption.
details: Metro rail services on the Uttara-Motijheel route were suspended for 26 minutes this morning after the lock on a train operator's cabin door opened mid-journey.
The incident occurred while a Motijheel-bound train was travelling between Shewrapara and Agargaon stations, according to MRT Police inspector (operations) Md Mohsin Sheikh.
The train reached Agargaon station at approximately 7:37 am, after which services were suspended as a safety precaution to address the issue.
Officials quickly fixed the problem, and train services resumed at 8:03 am.
Metro rail operations on the Uttara-Motijheel route have now returned to normal.

headline_marked: HRW: [[Three laws weaken human rights safeguards]] in Bangladesh
headline: HRW: Three laws weaken human rights safeguards in Bangladesh
summary: Human Rights Watch warns that new legislation regarding the NHRC, enforced disappearances, and the renamed RAB (now SRB) reverses key reforms.
details: Human Rights Watch (HRW) stated that three laws passed by parliament this month have weakened human rights safeguards and reversed reforms previously introduced by the interim government.
The legislation affects the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), enforced disappearances, and the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), which has been renamed the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
HRW reports that the new NHRC law reduces the commission's independence and investigative powers, requiring it to first seek reports from agencies before conducting its own inquiries.

The Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act removes the NHRC's power to inspect detention facilities and changes the standard for command responsibility, requiring direct orders for commander liability.
The Special Response Battalion Act replaces RAB with the SRB, transferring all personnel and powers while retaining the logo with only the name change.
HRW urged the government to introduce independent oversight and vetting for the SRB and called on the United States to maintain sanctions on the renamed force.
Asia director Elaine Pearson noted that Bangladesh needs real security sector reform and an independent human rights body to prevent a return to past abuses.
caption:
Three new laws have weakened human rights safeguards in Bangladesh, according to Human Rights Watch.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) stated that three laws passed by parliament this month have weakened human rights safeguards and reversed reforms previously introduced by the interim government.

The legislation affects the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), enforced disappearances, and the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), which has been renamed the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

HRW reports that the new NHRC law reduces the commission's independence and investigative powers, requiring it to first seek reports from agencies before conducting its own inquiries.

The Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act removes the NHRC's power to inspect detention facilities and changes the standard for command responsibility, requiring direct orders for commander liability.

The Special Response Battalion Act replaces RAB with the SRB, transferring all personnel and powers while retaining the logo with only the name change.

HRW urged the government to introduce independent oversight and vetting for the SRB and called on the United States to maintain sanctions on the renamed force.

Asia director Elaine Pearson noted that Bangladesh needs real security sector reform and an independent human rights body to prevent a return to past abuses.
